question.problem: Expressed as a fraction in lowest terms, $\frac{4}{3}÷2-\frac{1}{3}=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
To evaluate this expression, we use PEMDAS.

First, we divide:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3}÷2-\frac{1}{3} & = \\ (\frac{4}{3}÷\frac{2}{1})-\frac{1}{3} & = \\ (\frac{4}{3}\times \frac{1}{2})-\frac{1}{3} & = \\ (\frac{4\times 1}{3\times 2})-\frac{1}{3} & = \\ \frac{4}{6}-\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we subtract:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{6}-\frac{1}{3} & = \\ \frac{2}{3}-\frac{1}{3} & = \\ \frac{2-1}{3} & = \\ \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
